body.en: *Business* correspondence is written communication between businesses and with customers, banks and government. It gives a permanent record, can be used as evidence, reaches people far away and builds goodwill. A good business letter is clear, concise, correct, complete, courteous and considerate. Its parts are: letterhead (name, address and contact details of the sender), date, reference number, inside address (receiver's name and address), subject line, salutation (Dear Sir or Madam), body (opening, main message and closing), complimentary close (Yours faithfully or Yours sincerely), signature with name and designation, and enclosures where needed.

points.en: *Qualities*: clarity, conciseness, correctness, completeness, courtesy, consideration
Parts: letterhead, date, inside address, subject, salutation, body, close, signature
Enclosures and postscript only when needed

body.en: Common business *letters* include letters of enquiry (asking for information or prices), quotations (replying with prices and terms), orders, complaints and their adjustment, collection letters (asking for payment), and letters to banks, insurers and government. Job applications are also business letters. E-mail is now the main channel: it needs a clear subject line, a proper greeting, short paragraphs, correct attachments, a signature block, and care with tone, spelling and the reply-all button. Avoid writing in capital letters, which reads as shouting.

points.en: *E-mail*: clear subject, short, polite, check attachments

problem.en: Write the outline (not the full text) of a complaint letter from Sharma Stores to Kiran Electricals about 5 damaged fans in an order of 50.

steps.en: Letterhead of Sharma Stores; date; inside address of Kiran Electricals.
Subject: Damaged fans in our order no. 214. Salutation: Dear Sir or Madam.
Body: refer to the order and delivery date; state that 5 of 50 fans are damaged; enclose photos; request replacement or credit within a set time.
Close: Yours faithfully; signature, name and designation; enclosure: photographs.

answer.en: A polite, specific complaint with order details, the problem, evidence and the remedy wanted.
